label.claim: A Person of the measure of a thumb, like a light without smoke, is the Lord of past and future and abides within the self (atman).
label.A_quote: A Person of the measure of a thumb Stands in the midst of one's self (ātman), Lord of what has been and of what is to be.

label.claim: Book 3 is followed by the 'Criticism or Retraction concerning Magic' from his 'Declamation on the Uncertainty and Vanity of the Sciences' (Antwerp, 1531).
label.A_quote: Book 3 is followed at leaf F3 verso <note>the back side of the third leaf in the 'F' section of the book</note> by letters of Agrippa and, at leaf F6 verso, by the ‘Criticism or Retraction concerning Magic’ <note>original Latin: "Censura sive Retractatio De magia"</note>, from his ‘Declamation on the Uncertainty and Vanity of the Sciences’ <note>original Latin: "Declamatio de incertitudine et vanitate scientiarum"</note> (Antwerp, 1531).

label.claim: Ficino quotation on spirit and body accommodated to heavenly bodies through heat and moisture
label.A_quote: So that you may remember that our spirit and body—through a certain temperament tending toward heat and moisture, whether established by nature or sought through art—can be accommodated to the heavenly bodies and claim celestial gifts for itself.

label.claim: When thoughts are mastered by and fixed on the Real Self, the mind becomes steady like a lamp in a windless place and is satisfied seeing the Real Self by its own light.
label.A_quote: Then doth his mind become stable and steady, like the flame of the lamp which resteth in the place where no wind cometh to disturb or cause it to flicker.

label.claim: Petraeus wrote a "New Preface" for the 1717 Hamburg edition sharing information on the "reading and critique of alchemical writings," "histories of projection," and the "First Matter of the Philosophers."
label.A_quote: Nebst einer neuen Vorrede, Worinnen von Lesung und Critique der Alchymistischen Schrifften / ihren Scribenten, neuen Projections-Historien, der Materia Prima Philosophica, dem Leben des Basilii, und was in dieser Edition besonders præstiret worden, einige Nachricht mitgetheilet wird Von BENED. NIC. PETRÆO, Med. D.

label.claim: In the Western Galenic tradition, the primary tastes (sweet, sour, bitter, salty) were augmented by terms for fatty (unctuous) and bland (insipid) as flavors.
label.A_quote: For the unctuous <note>original: "unūuosa"; oily or fatty.</note> is more moderate; then follows the sweet, then the salty, and finally the styptic <note>a highly astringent taste that "contracts" the tissues of the mouth.</note>; after these, the insipid holds a middle place between these distances.

label.claim: The Hero Twins underwent the trial of the House of Bats in Xibalba, where they encountered the bat-god Camazotz.
label.A_quote: Hunahpu and Xbalanque, the heroes of the second book of the Popol Vuh, are here depicted undergoing the ordeal of the Bat House in the Mysteries of Xibalba.

label.claim: The particle of light waxes in size into an inner star, which is the form of the Lingadeha or sentient soul within the body.
label.A_quote: In this way, the single self becomes double, just as one sees his own death in a dream; it then waxes in size and thinks of its vital spark as a star. (This is the form of the <term>lingadeha</term>, or sentient soul within the body).

label.claim: Ma'at guided the creative words of Thoth and formulated the laws governing everything in heaven and earth.
label.A_quote: Thoth and Maāt were the chief agents who translated the will of Kheperȧ into action, and brought about the creation of the world; Thoth uttered the creative words, and Maāt guided the effects of them, and formulated the laws by which everything in heaven and in earth is ruled and governed.

label.claim: Based on Revelation 21:27, nothing that defiles through self-pollution shall enter the Heavenly Jerusalem, harming both body and spirit.
label.A_quote: There shall in no wise enter into the Heavenly Jerusalem, any thing that defileth, or worketh abomination.

label.claim: Ah Puch, the skeletal god of death, appears on Page 19 of the Dresden Codex
label.A_quote: The middle register shows two pairs of figures interacting, including a skeletal figure, with surrounding glyph blocks.

label.claim: In the Vendidad, emitting seed during sleep feeds the Drug, and reciting prayers like the Ahuna-Vairya upon waking counteracts it and destroys the demonic offspring.
label.A_quote: 49 (104). Then the Drug demon, the guileful one, answered: 'O holy, tall-formed Sraosha! this is the thing that counteracts it, namely, if the man, when he has risen from sleep, shall say three Ahuna-Vairya, two humatanãm, three hukhshathrô-temãm, and then chant the Ahuna-Vairya and offer up one Yênhê hâtãm.

label.claim: Waite notes that this restoration is the "logical succession" of the high degrees, moving the Mason from the earthly labor of the Craft to the spiritual realization of the Arch.
label.A_quote: *Lesson of the High Grades under the obedience of the Old Law—Concerning traces of the Secret Tradition—Claim of the Cryptic Degrees—The Royal Arch—An alternative concerning it—Its restoration of the lost secret—Whether it is a vain pretence—A profound intimation in the guise of commonplace—Whether that which is familiar can be informed with new meaning—The intimation conveyed in the secret according to the intention of those who devised the Grade—That intention was to lead apparently up to the Grade of Rose-Croix by shewing that the Mystery of Christ was the lost or interned part of the Masonic secret—Another side of the tradition concerning a loss in Israel—The cloud of Babylon on the Sanctuary—A difficulty concerning the Grades of Adonhiram—Our ignorance concerning the development of the Royal Arch—Dates which appear fairly certain—The Rose-Croix and the Cryptic Degrees—A void place which can only be filled by the Royal Arch—The logical succession of High Degrees—The Royal Arch*

label.claim: Mardana (Rubbing): Grinding mercury with minerals/substances to remove impurities
label.B_quote: Grinding with the specified medicines along with very sour <term>kanjika</term> is called <term>mardana</term>; it destroys impurities.

label.claim: Rasa-bandha (Bound Mercury) is the state where mercury is solidified and bound so it remains stable in fire.
label.A_quote: the fourth is the form-binding <note>original: <term>murtibandha</term></note>, and the fifth is the tablet-binding <note>original: <term>pattabandha</term></note>.
label.B_quote: Heavy, reddish, and in brilliance resembling the sun, it remains stable when held in the midst of fire; this is the characteristic of the Bound Form <note>term: "murtibandha" gloss: a solidified or "bound" state of mercury that resists heat</note>.

label.claim: Dennett's Nigerian Studies explores the connection between the Ifa divination system and the political organization of the Yoruba kingdom.
label.A_quote: These four great ones, the officers as it were of the first Ogboni, are compared to the complete Yoruba Kingdom, which they say was enclosed by four walls.
label.B_quote: The <term>Babalawo</term> Oliyitan described all the above as parts of Ifa, and as among these parts we find the ancestors of the Oyo, Egba, Ijebu and Iketu (the four walls of the Yoruba Kingdom), the connection between Ifa, the first <term>Oni</term>, and the walls is self-evident.

label.claim: Manly P. Hall's The Secret Teachings of All Ages (1928) is a landmark work distilling Pythagorean, Hermetic, and Rosicrucian thought into a single illustrated volume.
label.A_quote: Particular attention is paid to Neoplatonism; ancient Christianity; Rosicrucian and Freemasonic traditions; ancient mysteries; pagan rites and symbols; and Pythagorean mathematics.
label.B_quote: Between the covers of a single volume have been gathered those priceless secrets of an ancient learning, all of them susceptible of direct application to twentieth-century problems.

label.claim: AGLA is a Kabbalistic acronym formed from the initial letters of the Hebrew phrase Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai
label.A_quote: After this, you shall return to the eastern point and devoutly invoke the Great Name AGLA <note>AGLA is a Kabbalistic acronym for the Hebrew phrase Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai, meaning "You, O Lord, are mighty forever."</note>.
label.B_quote: For example, the name Agla <note>Hebrew: אגלא</note> is drawn from this verse of the Holy Scripture: Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai <note>Hebrew: אתה גיבר לעולם אדנו</note>, which is to say, "Thou art the mighty God for eternity."

label.claim: Murchana is defined as grinding mercury (e.g., with cow's urine and binding medicines) into a paste (pisti) to destroy defects of tin, lead, and arsenic, then raising (utthapana) or binding (bandhana) it into a solid mass.
label.A_quote: Ground with the urine of a cow that has never calved, it should be cooked in a <term>Valuka-yantra</term> <gloss>sand bath</gloss>.
label.B_quote: The process of grinding mercury with desired medicinal ingredients until it loses its original fluid form and becomes a paste is called <term>murchana</term> <gloss>swooning or fainting</gloss>.

label.claim: El abuso prolongado de la coca produce palidez y temblor de miembros, apetito errático e insomnio, reduciendo al coquero a un espectáculo miserable de disfrute antinatural que termina en años de miseria y una muerte dolorosa.
label.A_quote: As its stimulus is most fully developed when the body is exhausted with toil or the mind with conversation, "the victim then hastens to some retreat in a gloomy native wood, and flinging himself under a tree, remains stretched out there, heedless of night or of storms, unprotected by covering or by fire, unconscious of the floods of rain and of the tremendous winds which sweep the forest, and after yielding himself for two or three entire days to the occupation of chewing coca, returns home to his abode with trembling limbs and a pallid countenance—the miserable spectacle of unnatural enjoyment."
label.B_quote: The appetite becomes quite irregular, sometimes failing altogether, and sometimes assuming a wolfish voracity, especially for animal food.

label.claim: Plucking one string makes another string tuned to the unison vibrate on its own
label.A_quote: Now, one can hear this vibration; for if one plays the Lute, the Mandora <note>A small, pear-shaped stringed instrument from the lute family, popular in the Renaissance and Baroque periods.</note>, etc., the strings of the other instruments that happen to be at the unison of said strings or voices will respond to them.
label.B_quote: As for other strings that are not at the Unison, nor at the Octave, or at other Consonances <note>Musical intervals that sound harmonious and stable together, such as the Unison, Octave, or Fifth.</note> that cause strings to vibrate, they are never found in any disposition that is susceptible to the movement of the air pushed by the string one touches—as I will demonstrate in the discourse on the Octave.

label.claim: Carmina Gadelica contains instructions for a love charm using butterbur and foxglove
label.A_quote: Take with you the "peaked canopy" <gloss>butterbur</gloss>, <note>original: beannach pubaill</note> And the "priest's cap" <gloss>foxglove</gloss>. <note>original: currachd sagairt</note>
label.B_quote: <margin>[butterbur (?)]</margin>Take with you the "pointed canopy," <note>original: "beannach pubaill"; a traditional name for the butterbur plant</note> <margin>[foxglove (?)]</margin>    And the "priest's cap." <note>original: "currachd sagairt"; a traditional name for the foxglove</note>

label.claim: The Poimandres is the first book of the Corpus Hermeticum, detailing a vision of the creation of the universe and the fall of the Essential Man into matter.
label.B_quote: From such a great number, according to the opinion of Ficino <note>Marsilio Ficino (1433–1499), the Florentine priest and scholar who first translated the Hermetic corpus into Latin, fueling the Renaissance obsession with "ancient theology."</note>, only two survive: the <term>Poimandres</term> <note>The title of the first book of the Corpus Hermeticum, which describes a vision of the creation of the universe; Ficino used this title for the entire collection.</note> in Greek, and the Asclepius in Latin, which was translated long ago by Apuleius <note>The Roman author of The Golden Ass; in the Renaissance, he was traditionally but incorrectly believed to have translated the Hermetic dialogue Asclepius from Greek into Latin.</note>.

label.claim: Historical texts warned that masturbation in women caused 'hysterick fits', 'incurable jaundice', and 'barrenness' (infertility), withering the flower of youth.
label.A_quote: But what it produces more often than either is barrenness, a misfortune very afflictive to them, which cannot be redressed by either prayers or repentance.
label.B_quote: Besides all the symptoms I have already reported, women are more particularly exposed to fits of hysteria or frightful vapors, to incurable jaundice, to cruel cramps of the stomach and back;

label.claim: The Rosetta Stone calls King Ptolemy "beloved of Ptah" (meri-Ptah / Ptah meri) in his royal cartouche.
label.A_quote: nesu-bat Ptulmis ānkh djet Ptah meri {of the King of the South and North,} Ptolemy, {the ever-living,} {the beloved of Ptah,}

label.claim: Epictetus emphasizes focusing only on things within our own will and not letting external losses restrict the soul's freedom
label.A_quote: Appearances to the mind, a right use of them in our own power, i. 5; the standard of action, i. 93.

label.claim: Grafting an apple tree onto a plane tree (Platanus) produces bright red apples, and grafting it onto a poplar produces white fruit.

The Corpus Hermeticum texts attributed to Hermes Trismegistus (Thoth/Hermes) were written in the 2nd–3rd centuries CE and rediscovered and translated in the Renaissance, sparking an intellectual revolution.
label.A_quote: From such a great number, according to the opinion of Ficino <note>Marsilio Ficino (1433–1499), the Florentine priest and scholar who first translated the Hermetic corpus into Latin, fueling the Renaissance obsession with "ancient theology."</note>, only two survive: the <term>Poimandres</term> <note>The title of the first book of the Corpus Hermeticum, which describes a vision of the creation of the universe; Ficino used this title for the entire collection.</note> in Greek, and the Asclepius in Latin, which was translated long ago by Apuleius <note>The Roman author of The Golden Ass; in the Renaissance, he was traditionally but incorrectly believed to have translated the Hermetic dialogue Asclepius from Greek into Latin.</note>.

label.claim: The Sweet (Madhura) category in Ayurveda includes meats, fats, and milk, described as unctuous, heavy, and building for the body's tissues.
Lilith manifests in dreams to cause nocturnal emissions as a profane spiritual union that weakens a man's soul and chains him to the lower spheres
The aura becomes sticky and attracts entities that feed on anxiety and fear, draining energy and making the personality selfish or cold (and physically the heart and lungs work at an unnatural pace).
label.A_quote: The horrors which torment a man suffering from delirium tremens are largely due to the sight of the loathsome elementals that gather round places where liquor is sold, and feed on its exhalations, and are attracted round him by the effluvia of his own drink-sodden body.

label.claim: To join their assembly and see them (unless they will it), one must be able to perceive this supernatural light.
The Fourth Book of Occult Philosophy is a practical manual on ceremonial magic distinct from the theoretical first three books.
label.A_quote: HENRY CORNELIUS AGRIPPA’S FOURTH BOOK ON OCCULT PHIlosophy, or on Ceremonial Magic. <note>original: "De Occulta Philosophia, seu de Cerimoniis Magicis." This title distinguishes this practical manual of ritual from the more theoretical approach of the first three books.</note>

label.claim: In Papus's system, the number 2 represents the Binah (Understanding) principle—the feminine, receptive vessel that gives birth to ideas.
label.A_quote: to all the passive significations emanated from the Binary; hence the ideas of reflection, of Woman, applied to the Moon relatively to the Sun and to Woman relatively to Man.

label.claim: Music makes the spirits thinner, swifter, and warmer, thereby dissipating heavy humors like black bile to uplift the mind.
label.A_quote: Since this happens for the benefit of the spirits, which, being rendered thinner, swifter, and warmer, dissipate and attenuate or mitigate those humors by which diseases were generated, and consequently turn the mind and imagination away for a time from the apprehension of the disease that afflicts the soul more than is fitting, they exhilarate it so much that they assign all the excited spirits to repelling the infirmity.

label.claim: Jean Ruel states that apples should be picked by hand without shaking the tree and stored in barley straw or wrapped individually in vine leaves to retain moisture.
